questions.question: The sum of five numbers is 655. The average of the first two numbers is 77 and the third number is 101. Find the average of the remaining two numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Sum of last two numbers** = Total Sum − (Sum of first two + Third number)

Sum of last two = 655 − (77 × 2 + 101)

Sum of last two = 655 − (154 + 101) = 655 − 255 = 400

**Required Average** = 400 ÷ 2 = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Sum of 5 numbers** = 655

**Average of 1st and 2ⁿd number** = 77

**Value of 3rd number** = 101

**Formula Used:**

Sum = Average × Number of observations

Average = Sum ÷ Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c3fcaa6755622fe8c8aea3e6a2799ab101898355a7fb95161d8d58756f89bb61.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of first two numbers = 77 × 2 = 154

⇒ Sum of first three numbers = 154 + 101 = 255

⇒ Sum of remaining two numbers = Total Sum − Sum of first three numbers

⇒ Sum of remaining two numbers = 655 − 255 = 400

⇒ Average of remaining two numbers = 400 ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Definition of Average

Average is the **central value** of a set of data, calculated by dividing the total sum of values by the number of values.

Properties of Averages

If every number in a set is increased or decreased by a constant **'k'**, the average also increases or decreases by **'k'**.

Weighted Average

When groups have different sizes, the combined average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: The average marks of 30 students in a mathematics test were found to be 55. However, it was later discovered that a mark of 72 was mistakenly recorded as 27, and another mark of 64 was mistakenly recorded as 46. What is the actual average score?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Net change** in marks = (Correct marks) − (Incorrect marks)

Net change = (72 + 64) − (27 + 46) = 136 − 73 = **+63**

Average **deviation** = 63 ÷ 30 = **2.1**

Actual Average = Initial Average + Deviation = 55 + 2.1 = **57.1**

**∴ The correct answer is 57.1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total students = 30, Initial average = 55, Errors = (27 instead of 72) and (46 instead of 64).

**Formula:** Correct Average = (Correct Sum of Observations) ÷ (Number of Observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/53e85f48d4c92c8f38581de3fc2d71ba131eadadd27641d2f8e7c1e9d33604a6.png] 

⇒ Initial Total Marks = 30 × 55 = 1650

⇒ Correct Total Marks = 1650 − (27 + 46) + (72 + 64)

⇒ Correct Total Marks = 1650 − 73 + 136

⇒ Correct Total Marks = 1713

⇒ Actual Average = 1713 ÷ 30

⇒ Actual Average = 57.1

**∴ The correct answer is 57.1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Average (Arithmetic Mean)

If every observation in a set is increased or decreased by a constant value **k**, the new average will also increase or decrease by **k**.

Net Deviation Rule

The sum of **deviations** of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always **zero**. This principle helps in quickly finding missing values or correcting errors.

Weighted Average

When two or more groups are combined, the combined average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where **n** is the count and **x** is the average of each group.</p

questions.question: A student scores 80 marks in a subject with a weightage of 3 and 90 marks in another subject with a weightage of 2. What is the weighted average score of the student?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Weighted Average** = (Value₁ × w₁ + Value₂ × w₂) ÷ (w₁ + w₂)

Sum = (80 × 3) + (90 × 2) = 240 + 180 = 420

Total Weight = 3 + 2 = 5

Weighted Average = 420 ÷ 5 = 84

**∴ The correct answer is 84 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Score 1 = **80** (Weightage = **3**), Score 2 = **90** (Weightage = **2**).

**Formula Used:** Weighted Average = Σ (Weight × Score) ÷ Σ (Weight)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8522bb348f12ea2b38e805f32edcbd3dca378ccbdd17fbdcd133d4fb5e1b91f4.png] 

⇒ Total Marks = (80 × 3) + (90 × 2)

⇒ Total Marks = 240 + 180 = 420

⇒ Total Weightage = 3 + 2 = 5

⇒ Weighted Average = 420 ÷ 5

⇒ Weighted Average = 84

**∴ The correct answer is 84 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

It is calculated as (w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + ... + wₙxₙ) ÷ (w₁ + w₂ + ... + wₙ), where x represents values and w represents their respective weights.

Comparison with Simple Average

A **Simple Average** is a special case of the weighted average where all weights are equal (w₁ = w₂ = ... = wₙ).

Combined Mean

If two groups have sizes n₁, n₂ and averages x₁, x₂, the **Combined Mean** is (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: The average of 6 numbers is 18. If each number is increased by 5, what will be the new average?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Property: If each **observation** in a data set is increased by a constant **k**, the **mean average** of the set also increases by exactly **k**.

New Average = **Old Average** + **Increase Value**

⇒ New Average = 18 + 5 = 23

**∴ The correct answer is 23.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Number of observations = 6 | Original average = 18 | Increase per number = 5

**Formula Used:** Average = Sum of observations ÷ Total number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/80482217760a766a1d94117cb53ef690171336fa0605a1cdea46918a4716e121.png] 

⇒ Sum of original 6 numbers = 18 × 6 = 108

⇒ Total increase after adding 5 to each number = 5 × 6 = 30

⇒ New Total Sum = 108 + 30 = 138

⇒ New Average = 138 ÷ 6 = 23

**∴ The correct answer is 23.**

**__Additional Information__**

Effect of Operations on Average

If every term is multiplied by **k**, the average is multiplied by **k**. If every term is divided by **k**, the average is divided by **k**.

Average of Consecutive Numbers

The average of **n** consecutive numbers is the middle term if **n** is odd, or the mean of the two middle terms if **n** is even.

Weighted Average Formula

Weighted Average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), used when combining two groups with different averages.</p

questions.question: The average weight of M and his three friends is 65 kg. If M's weight is 8 kg more than the average weight of his three friends, what is M's weight (in kg)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total weight of all 4 people = 65 × 4 = 260 kg.

Let the **average weight** of the 3 friends be x kg.

M's weight = x + 8 kg.

Sum of weights = 3x + (x + 8) = 260 ⇒ 4x = 252 ⇒ x = 63 kg.

M's weight = 63 + 8 = 71 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 71 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of **M and 3 friends** (Total 4 people) = 65 kg.

Difference between **M's weight** and the average of 3 friends = 8 kg.

**Formula Used:**

Total Sum = Average × Number of entities

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/390ce84f4e43c8da67acf23f56886af504f2f57eb984ab1f5f06b8e5e384443f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of M + 3 friends = 4 × 65 = 260 kg

⇒ Let the average weight of 3 friends be A kg.

⇒ Weight of M = A + 8 kg

⇒ Sum of weight of 3 friends = 3 × A

⇒ Total Weight = (Sum of 3 friends) + (Weight of M)

⇒ 260 = 3A + (A + 8)

⇒ 260 = 4A + 8

⇒ 4A = 260 − 8

⇒ 4A = 252

⇒ A = 252 ÷ 4 = 63 kg

⇒ M's weight = A + 8 = 63 + 8 = 71 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 71 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When groups with different averages are combined, the total average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Average Deviation

The sum of deviations of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero.

Arithmetic Mean

Mean = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations).</p

questions.question: In a class of 30 students, the average score on a test is 75. If 20 students scored an average of 80, what is the average score of the remaining 10 students?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **overall average** of 30 students is 75.

The first **20 students** have an average of 80, which is +5 more than the **total average**.

Total excess score = 20 × 5 = +100.

To balance this, the remaining **10 students** must have a total deficit of −100.

Average of remaining 10 students = 75 + (−100 ÷ 10) = 65.

**∴ The correct answer is 65.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of **students** = 30

Average score of **class** = 75

Average score of **20 students** = 80

**Formula Used:**

Sum of values = Average × Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0ac5bb14d4400b0223c894a2271e13c4874127ca6e84c3f69e5f60d837f50113.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total score of all 30 students = 30 × 75 = 2250

⇒ Total score of 20 students = 20 × 80 = 1600

⇒ Total score of remaining 10 students = 2250 − 1600 = 650

⇒ Average score of remaining 10 students = 650 ÷ 10 = 65

**∴ The correct answer is 65.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

When two groups with averages a₁ and a₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, the new average is (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Net Deviation Rule

The sum of the **deviations** of all items in a set from their **arithmetic mean** is always zero.

Constant Change

If every value in a data set is increased or decreased by a constant 'k', the **average** of the set also increases or decreases by 'k'.</p

questions.question: The average age of Amit, Arjun and Anya is 30 years. If the average age of Amit and Anya is 35 years, what will be Arjun's age after 2 years?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total age of **Amit, Arjun, and Anya** = 30 × 3 = 90 years

Total age of **Amit and Anya** = 35 × 2 = 70 years

**Arjun's present age** = 90 − 70 = 20 years

**Arjun's age after 2 years** = 20 + 2 = 22 years

**∴ The correct answer is 22 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average age of **Amit, Arjun, and Anya** = 30 years

Average age of **Amit and Anya** = 35 years

**Formula Used:**

Total Sum = **Average × Number of observations**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/96e63e4789504190cc7edad8bbcd8ddef0add2d86e63172f4cd51cc6a9f6aa25.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total age of Amit, Arjun, and Anya = 30 × 3 = 90 years

⇒ Total age of Amit and Anya = 35 × 2 = 70 years

⇒ **Arjun's present age** = (Amit + Arjun + Anya) − (Amit + Anya)

⇒ Arjun's present age = 90 − 70 = 20 years

⇒ Arjun's age after 2 years = 20 + 2 = 22 years

**∴ The correct answer is 22 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Average Formula

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Number of observations). To find the sum, use: **Sum = Average × Count**.

Age Increment Property

If the age of every person in a group increases by **n years**, the average age of the group also increases by **n years**.

Exclusion Principle

Age of excluded member = (Initial Sum) − (New Sum). This is used when one person leaves the group and the average changes.</p

questions.question: A shop sells candles in two packs: Pack A: 5 candles at ₹4 each and Pack B: 5 candles at ₹6 each. What is the average price per candle?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Since the quantity of candles in both packs is equal (5 candles each), the average price is the simple arithmetic mean of the individual prices.

Average Price = (₹4 + ₹6) ÷ 2

Average Price = ₹10 ÷ 2 = ₹5

**∴ The correct option is B.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Pack A has 5 candles at ₹4 each and Pack B has 5 candles at ₹6 each.

Formula Used: Average Price = Total Cost ÷ Total Quantity

 
• 
 
 Pack A
 5 × ₹4
 
 Pack B
 5 × ₹6
 

 Average Price = ₹5

⇒ Total number of candles = 5 + 5 = 10

⇒ Total cost of Pack A = 5 × 4 = ₹20

⇒ Total cost of Pack B = 5 × 6 = ₹30

⇒ Total cost of both packs = 20 + 30 = ₹50

⇒ Average price = 50 ÷ 10 = ₹5

**∴ The correct option is B.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

When quantities are different, use Average = (n₁w₁ + n₂w₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is quantity and w is value.

Arithmetic Mean for Equal Weights

If n₁ = n₂ = n₃..., the weighted average simplifies to the basic average of the values: (w₁ + w₂ + ... + wₖ) ÷ k.

Unitary Method in Price

Total Cost = Number of Units × Price per Unit. To find the average, always divide the total sum of costs by the total sum of units.

questions.question: A group of people consists of men, women and children. Among them, 20% are men, 30% are women and the rest are children, and their average weights are 50 kg, 40 kg and 40 kg, respectively. The average weight of the group (in kg) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Men** : **Women** : **Children** = 20 : 30 : 50 = 2 : 3 : 5.

Total weighted sum = (2 × 50) + (3 × 40) + (5 × 40) = 100 + 120 + 200 = 420.

Average weight of group = 420 ÷ (2 + 3 + 5) = 42 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage of **Men** = 20%, **Women** = 30%.

Average weights: **Men** = 50 kg, **Women** = 40 kg, **Children** = 40 kg.

**Formula:**

Average Weight = (Total Weight of all People) ÷ (Total Number of People)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5504e8f394d215f8e7b348af6677c1d046f9cf55b68b4a5c3469ff839ee03e24.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Percentage of **Children** = 100% − (20% + 30%) = 50%

⇒ Let total number of people in the group = 100

⇒ Number of Men = 20, Women = 30, Children = 50

⇒ Total weight = (20 × 50) + (30 × 40) + (50 × 40)

⇒ Total weight = 1000 + 1200 + 2000 = 4200 kg

⇒ Average weight of the group = 4200 ÷ 100 = 42 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 42 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

It is the average of a data set where different values have different levels of importance or frequency. Formula: Average = (n₁w₁ + n₂w₂ + ...) ÷ (n₁ + n₂ + ...).

Deviation Method

Pick an assumed average (e.g., 40) and calculate the net deviation. Here, 20% are +10 above 40, so Net Deviation = 20 × 10 = 200. Final Average = 40 + (200 ÷ 100) = 42 kg.</p

questions.question: A group of people consists of men, women and children. Among them, 20% are men, 30% are women and the rest are children, and their average weights are 50 kg, 40 kg and 30 kg, respectively. The average weight of the group (in kg) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Men** : **Women** : **Children** = 20% : 30% : 50% = 2 : 3 : 5

Multiply the ratio units by their respective **average weights**:

Sum = (2 × 50) + (3 × 40) + (5 × 30) = 100 + 120 + 150 = 370

Average of the **group** = Total Sum ÷ Total Ratio units = 370 ÷ 10 = 37 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 37 kg.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage of **Men** = 20% | **Average weight** = 50 kg

Percentage of **Women** = 30% | **Average weight** = 40 kg

Percentage of **Children** = 100% − (20% + 30%) = 50% | **Average weight** = 30 kg

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/65196577007739c1d99a0d661b5bbe20b9006bfbab086e1f8878339ee538632a.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = (n₁ × x₁ + n₂ × x₂ + n₃ × x₃) ÷ (n₁ + n₂ + n₃)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total number of people in the **group** be 100.

⇒ Number of **Men** = 20, **Women** = 30, **Children** = 50.

⇒ Total weight of Men = 20 × 50 = 1000 kg.

⇒ Total weight of Women = 30 × 40 = 1200 kg.

⇒ Total weight of Children = 50 × 30 = 1500 kg.

⇒ Total weight of the group = 1000 + 1200 + 1500 = 3700 kg.

⇒ Average weight of the group = 3700 ÷ 100 = 37 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 37 kg.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

It is used when components of a group have different weights or frequencies. Formula: Aₐvg = (Σnᵢ × xᵢ) ÷ Σnᵢ.

Deviation Method

Assume a mean (e.g., 40) and calculate the net deviation: 20%(+10) + 30%(0) + 50%(−10). Net = +2 − 5 = −3. Final Avg = 40 − 3 = 37 kg.

Ratio Property of Averages

The average of a group remains unchanged if the number of members in each sub-group is scaled by the same ratio constant.</p

questions.question: The average of first 17 multiples of 13 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **average** of the first **n multiples** of a number **x** is given by the formula: **x × (n + 1) ÷ 2**.

In this question, **x = 13** and **n = 17**.

⇒ Average = 13 × (17 + 1) ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 13 × 18 ÷ 2 = 13 × 9 = 117

**∴ The correct answer is 117.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of terms (n) = 17

Multiplier = 13

The sequence is: 13, 26, 39, ..., (13 × 17)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3f46658c9b1c1fee060695905f122f6f35ff9d7e21e9e08e2632aab38cf66599.png] 

**Formula Used:**

For an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)**, the **Average** = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

**Calculations:**

⇒ First term (a) = 13 × 1 = 13

⇒ Last term (l) = 13 × 17 = 221

⇒ Average = (13 + 221) ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 234 ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 117

**∴ The correct answer is 117.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of AP

In any series with a common difference, the **average** is always the **middle term** if the number of terms is odd, calculated as (n + 1)/2 th term.

Sum of AP

The sum of an AP is Sₙ = n/2 × [2a + (n − 1)d] or Sₙ = n/2 × [first term + last term].

Average of first n Natural Numbers

The average of the first **n** natural numbers is (n + 1) ÷ 2. For multiples of **k**, just multiply this average by **k**.</p

questions.question: A class of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 70, and that of the rest is 62. What is the average score of the class?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Ratio** of **students** = 12 : 18 = 2 : 3

Difference between **averages** = 70 − 62 = 8

Apply **Net Deviation** (taking 62 as base): (2 × 8) ÷ (2 + 3) = 16 ÷ 5 = 3.2

**Class Average** = 62 + 3.2 = 65.2

**∴ The correct answer is 65.2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total students (n) = 30

Group 1: **Students** (n₁) = 12, **Average** (a₁) = 70

Group 2: **Students** (n₂) = 30 − 12 = 18, **Average** (a₂) = 62

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9ec92059a03455c5121f7596a05b6b6d039298ddd3a02e9df403abba8a24885c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total score** of 12 students = 12 × 70 = 840

⇒ **Total score** of 18 students = 18 × 62 = 1116

⇒ **Sum** of all scores = 840 + 1116 = 1956

⇒ **Average score** of the class = 1956 ÷ 30

⇒ Average score = 65.2

**∴ The correct answer is 65.2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When a group is divided into subgroups with different averages, the combined average is the sum of (number × average) of each subgroup divided by the total count.

Net Deviation Method

To simplify calculations, assume a **base average** (usually the smaller value). The actual average = Base + (Net Deviation ÷ Total observations).

Arithmetic Mean

The most basic average type, calculated as Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations. Formula: μ = (Σxᵢ) ÷ n.</p

questions.question: The average age of 4 people is 52 years. Another group has 6 people with an average age of 58 years. When both groups are combined, what is the average age of all the people?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **number of people** = 4 : 6 ⇒ 2 : 3.

Assume **base average** = 52. Difference in **average** = 58 − 52 = +6.

Net **deviation** to be distributed = 3 parts × 6 = 18.

Average **deviation** = 18 ÷ (2 + 3) = 18 ÷ 5 = 3.6.

**Combined average** = 52 + 3.6 = 55.6 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 55.6 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Average age** of first group (n₁=4) is 52 years, **Average age** of second group (n₂=6) is 58 years.

**Formula Used:** **Combined Average** = (n₁ × Avg₁ + n₂ × Avg₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69cc279c5eb4ef19c878bed31661936b32425ae5618a214fe2042a5fa5ec4796.png] 

⇒ **Total age** of Group 1 = 4 × 52 = 208 years.

⇒ **Total age** of Group 2 = 6 × 58 = 348 years.

⇒ **Combined sum** of ages = 208 + 348 = 556 years.

⇒ **Total number of people** = 4 + 6 = 10 people.

⇒ **Overall Average** = 556 ÷ 10 = 55.6 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 55.6 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

It is used to find the **average** of two or more groups with different sizes: A꜀ₒₘbᵢₙₑd = (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂ + ...) ÷ (n₁ + n₂ + ...).

Deviation Method

Assumed Average + (Net Deviation ÷ Total Count). This method simplifies calculations by reducing the size of **multiplication** factors.

Weighted Average Property

The **combined average** always lies between the smallest and the largest **individual averages** of the groups.</p

questions.question: The average of 10 observations is 40. It was realised later that an observation was misread as 32 in place of 43. Find the correct average.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net change in **Sum** = **Correct value** − **Wrong value** = 43 − 32 = +11

Change in **Average** = Net change in Sum ÷ Total observations = 11 ÷ 10 = +1.1

**Correct Average** = Old Average + Change in Average = 40 + 1.1 = 41.1

**∴ The correct answer is 41.1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Total observations** (n) = 10 | **Old Average** = 40 | **Wrong value** = 32 | **Correct value** = 43

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a3f2ce428fbd3564c7194d2695b223332820bfc9514f5135ae9489205d353f9.png] 

**Formula:** **Correct Average** = (**Old Sum** − **Wrong Value** + **Correct Value**) ÷ n

⇒ **Old Sum** = Average × Number of observations = 40 × 10 = 400

⇒ **Correct Sum** = 400 − 32 + 43

⇒ **Correct Sum** = 411

⇒ **Correct Average** = 411 ÷ 10

⇒ **Correct Average** = 41.1

**∴ The correct answer is 41.1.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Arithmetic Mean Property

If each observation is increased by a constant value 'k', the **new average** also increases by 'k'. If multiplied by 'k', the new average becomes **old average × k**.

Correction Formula

Correct Average = Old Average + (Sum of Correct items − Sum of Incorrect items) ÷ Total items.</p

questions.question: If the average of 6 consecutive odd numbers is 30, the difference between the largest and the smallest numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **n consecutive odd or even numbers**, the **difference** between the **largest** and **smallest** number is always 2 × (n − 1).

In this case, n = 6.

⇒ Difference = 2 × (6 − 1)

⇒ Difference = 2 × 5 = 10

Note: The **average** value (30) does not affect the **difference** between the numbers.

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average of **6 consecutive odd numbers** = 30.

The **average** of an even count of consecutive numbers is the **middle point** between the two center-most numbers.

⇒ Middle two numbers are 30 − 1 and 30 + 1 (since they are odd).

⇒ 3rd number = 29 and 4th number = 31.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/325fd5823e2b90831d15f2e6a240e5663fcc55c65fc75097b6ee08b34c8a9410.png] 

By finding all numbers in the sequence:

⇒ Sequence: 25, 27, 29, 31, 33, 35

⇒ **Smallest number** = 25

⇒ **Largest number** = 35

⇒ **Difference** = 35 − 25 = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of Consecutive Numbers

For an **odd number of terms**, the average is the **middle term** itself. For an **even number of terms**, the average is the mean of the **two middle terms**.

Difference Property

In any **Arithmetic Progression (AP)** with common difference 'd' and 'n' terms, the difference between the **first and last term** is always (n − 1) × d.

Sum of First n Odd Numbers

The sum of the first 'n' odd natural numbers starting from 1 is always n².</p

questions.question: The average of five numbers is 56. Four of the numbers are 35, 42, 32, and 26. What is the fifth number?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume the base **average** is 56.

Calculate **deviations** of given numbers: (35−56) + (42−56) + (32−56) + (26−56)

⇒ −21 + (−14) + (−24) + (−30) = **−89**.

To maintain the average of 56, the fifth number must balance this by being **89 more** than the average.

Fifth number = 56 + 89 = **145**.

**∴ The correct answer is 145.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average of **5 numbers** = 56. Known numbers = **35, 42, 32, 26**.

**Formula Used:** Sum of observations = **Average × Number of observations**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c09d71cd3fdf472f5dc3b2263d4ca27d2678c50a8cf0d0ef67d18f1c5a91f3a3.png] 

⇒ Total sum of all 5 numbers = 56 × 5 = **280**

⇒ Sum of the 4 given numbers = 35 + 42 + 32 + 26 = **135**

⇒ Let the fifth number be **x**.

⇒ 135 + x = 280

⇒ x = 280 − 135

⇒ x = 145

**∴ The correct answer is 145.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Property

The algebraic sum of **deviations** of a set of observations from their **arithmetic mean** is always **zero**.

Inclusion/Exclusion Rule

New Value = (New Average × New Quantity) − (Old Average × Old Quantity).

Average of AP

For numbers in **Arithmetic Progression**, Average = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.</p

questions.question: There are two sections A and B of a class, consisting of 22 and 44 students, respectively. If the average weight of section A is 40 kg and that of section B is 37 kg, find the average weight of the whole class (in kg).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **students** in Section A to Section B = 22 : 44 = 1 : 2.

Weight of **Section A** is 40 kg and **Section B** is 37 kg.

Assume 37 kg as **base weight**; Deviation for Section A = 40 − 37 = +3 kg.

Net deviation distributed over total ratio parts = (1 × 3) ÷ (1 + 2) = 3 ÷ 3 = 1 kg.

Required **Average Weight** = 37 + 1 = 38 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 38 kg.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of students in **Section A** (n₁) = 22

Average weight of **Section A** (w₁) = 40 kg

Number of students in **Section B** (n₂) = 44

Average weight of **Section B** (w₂) = 37 kg

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = (n₁w₁ + n₂w₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7d451ee0fd5ca45716a334f7625181417c80df3e566e8c2026e99bc019acb55e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of **Section A** = 22 × 40 = 880 kg

⇒ Total weight of **Section B** = 44 × 37 = 1628 kg

⇒ Total weight of the whole **class** = 880 + 1628 = 2508 kg

⇒ Total number of **students** = 22 + 44 = 66

⇒ Average weight of the **class** = 2508 ÷ 66

⇒ Average weight = 38 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 38 kg.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Principle

When two groups are combined, the resulting average always lies between the averages of the individual groups. It is closer to the average of the group with more members.

Ratio Method for Averages

Instead of using actual student counts, the **ratio of quantities** can be used in the formula: Average = (R₁A₁ + R₂A₂) ÷ (R₁ + R₂), where R represents the ratio parts.

Deviation Concept

Net Deviation = Sum of (Value − Assumed Average). For the final average, the net deviation must be zero across all items.</p

questions.question: The average of fifty numbers is 34. If two numbers, namely 34 and 22 are discarded, the average of the remaining numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Discarding **34** (which is the **original average**) doesn't change the average of the remaining 49 numbers.

Discarding **22**, which is (34 − 22) = **12** less than the average, creates a **surplus**.

This surplus is distributed over the remaining (50 − 2) = **48** numbers.

Increase in **Average** = 12 ÷ 48 = **0.25**.

New **Average** = 34 + 0.25 = **34.25**.

**∴ The correct answer is 34.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The average of **50 numbers** is **34**. Two numbers, **34** and **22**, are discarded.

**Formula Used:** Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/28aedbc3e3f9288b686f7abe6049a74b537bbcbc6430879772b12c29c42e7ba1.png] 

⇒ **Initial Total Sum** = Average × Count = 34 × 50 = **1700**

⇒ Sum of discarded numbers = 34 + 22 = **56**

⇒ **New Sum** after discarding = 1700 − 56 = **1644**

⇒ **New Count** of numbers = 50 − 2 = **48**

⇒ **New Average** = New Sum ÷ New Count = 1644 ÷ 48

⇒ New Average = **34.25**

**∴ The correct answer is 34.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Property of Average when removing values

If the discarded number is **greater** than the average, the new average **decreases**. If the discarded number is **smaller** than the average, the new average **increases**.

Uniform Change

If every number in a set is increased or decreased by a constant **k**, the **average** also increases or decreases by **k** respectively.

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and counts n₁ and n₂ are combined, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: The average of 10 observations is 40. It was realised later that an observation was misread as 31 in place of 50. Find the correct average.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net difference in observations = **Correct value** − **Incorrect value** = 50 − 31 = +19.

Adjustment in average = Net difference ÷ **Total observations** = 19 ÷ 10 = +1.9.

Correct average = **Old Average** + Adjustment = 40 + 1.9 = 41.9.

**∴ The correct answer is 41.9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of observations (n) = 10

Initial **Average** = 40

**Incorrect observation** = 31

**Correct observation** = 50

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations

Correct Sum = (Initial Average × n) − Incorrect Value + Correct Value

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36696c1646c6422d04192d7ce4c81b8f422c0796d714552e3d3994f94a5e6b09.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Sum = 40 × 10 = 400

⇒ Correct Sum = 400 − 31 + 50

⇒ Correct Sum = 369 + 50 = 419

⇒ Correct Average = 419 ÷ 10

⇒ Correct Average = 41.9

**∴ The correct answer is 41.9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effect of Change on Average

If each observation is increased or decreased by a constant 'k', the average also increases or decreases by 'k'. New Average = Old Average ± k.

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Net Deviation Method

The sum of deviations of all observations from their mean is always zero. This property is used to quickly find missing values or corrections.</p

questions.question: The average weight of A, B and C is 45 kg. If the average weight of A and B is 37 kg and that of B and C is 47 kg, then the weight of B (in kg) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Weight of **B** = (Sum of **A and B**) + (Sum of **B and C**) − (Total Sum of **A, B and C**)

Weight of **B** = (37 × 2) + (47 × 2) − (45 × 3)

Weight of **B** = 74 + 94 − 135 = 33 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 33 kg.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of **A, B and C** = 45 kg

Average weight of **A and B** = 37 kg

Average weight of **B and C** = 47 kg

**Formula Used:**

**Sum of observations** = **Average** × **Total number of observations**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b2d3ea1a6a9cde0495bdb5631d420a5e6fefd1234d33de65cc55df9b19f3cea4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of **A, B and C** = 45 × 3 = 135 kg

⇒ Total weight of **A and B** = 37 × 2 = 74 kg

⇒ Total weight of **B and C** = 47 × 2 = 94 kg

⇒ Sum of (A + B) and (B + C) = A + 2B + C = 74 + 94 = 168 kg

⇒ Weight of **B** = (A + 2B + C) − (A + B + C)

⇒ Weight of **B** = 168 − 135 = 33 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 33 kg.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average of Group

The average of a group is the sum of all values divided by the number of values in that group. Formula: Average = Sum ÷ n.

Overlap Method

In problems where one person is part of two subgroups, their value = (Sum of subgroup 1 + Sum of subgroup 2) − (Total sum of all members).

Excluded Value

Weight of an excluded person = (Initial Total Weight) − (New Total Weight after exclusion).</p

questions.question: The average of three numbers is 154. The first number is twice the second number, and the second number is twice the third number. What is the first number?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **1st** : **2ⁿd** : **3rd** numbers = 4 : 2 : 1.

Total sum = 154 × 3 = 462.

Sum of ratio parts = 4 + 2 + 1 = 7 units.

7 units = 462 ⇒ 1 unit = 66.

**First number** = 4 units = 4 × 66 = 264.

**∴ The correct answer is 264.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Average of three numbers** = 154.

**Formula Used:** **Sum** = **Average** × **Total Count of Numbers**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f5d00e623478a719f5f581695569ea58352a8a5e150c182d92b6aabd0a8e93d6.png] 

Let the **third number** be x.

⇒ **Second number** = 2 × x = 2x.

⇒ **First number** = 2 × 2x = 4x.

⇒ **Sum of the three numbers** = x + 2x + 4x = 7x.

⇒ Total Sum = 154 × 3 = 462.

⇒ 7x = 462

⇒ x = 462 ÷ 7 = 66.

⇒ **First number** = 4x = 4 × 66 = 264.

**∴ The correct answer is 264.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average or Arithmetic Mean

The average of n terms is the sum of terms divided by n. Sum = Average × n.

Ratio Scaling

When numbers are multiples of each other, assigning the smallest value as 1 unit helps in establishing a quick **ratio chain**.

Linear Equations in One Variable

Expressing all unknown values in terms of a single variable (x) simplifies the calculation of the **sum** or **product**.</p

questions.question: A class of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 70, and that of the rest is 64. What is the average score of the class?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **students** = 12 : 18 = 2 : 3.

Using the **weighted average** method: [(2 × 70) + (3 × 64)] ÷ (2 + 3)

⇒ (140 + 192) ÷ 5 = 332 ÷ 5 = 66.4.

**∴ The correct answer is 66.4.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca3b8bd042a8593847c9ff473103b3431c8bb59eb83a64a3c74be0954b4c8d19.png] 

**Given:**

**Total students** in the class = 30.

Number of **first group** (n₁) = 12 students, **Average score** (A₁) = 70.

Number of **second group** (n₂) = 30 − 12 = 18 students, **Average score** (A₂) = 64.

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total score** of 12 students = 12 × 70 = 840.

⇒ **Total score** of remaining 18 students = 18 × 64 = 1152.

⇒ **Total score** of the entire class = 840 + 1152 = 1992.

⇒ **Average score** of the class = 1992 ÷ 30.

⇒ **Average score** of the class = 66.4.

**∴ The correct answer is 66.4.**

**__Additional Information__**

Combined Average Formula

The combined average of multiple groups is calculated as A = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂ + ... + nₖAₖ) ÷ (n₁ + n₂ + ... + nₖ).

Deviation Method (Assumed Mean)

Pick an **assumed average** (a), then New Average = a + (Total Deviation ÷ Total Number). For this problem, if a = 64, deviation = [12 × (70 − 64)] ÷ 30 = 72 ÷ 30 = 2.4. So, 64 + 2.4 = 66.4.

Weighted Average Principle

When the size of groups is different, the **group average** with more members will pull the overall **class average** closer to its value.</p

questions.question: The average weight of 14 boys in a class is 40.25 kg and that of the remaining 4 boys is 38 kg. Find the average weight (in kg, rounded off to two decimal place) of all the boys in the class.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **number of boys** = 14 : 4 = 7 : 2.

Assume **base average** = 38 kg.

Deviation of 14 boys = 40.25 − 38 = +2.25 kg.

Total deviation = 14 × 2.25 = 31.5 kg.

Average increase = 31.5 ÷ 18 = 1.75 kg.

**Final Average** = 38 + 1.75 = 39.75 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 39.75 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Average weight** of first 14 boys = 40.25 kg

**Average weight** of remaining 4 boys = 38 kg

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d9059688428a78b35b029fa31eec6144b23c0f90cdc4ad58ec6e363257877fd7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total weight** of 14 boys = 14 × 40.25 = 563.5 kg

⇒ **Total weight** of 4 boys = 4 × 38 = 152 kg

⇒ **Total number of boys** = 14 + 4 = 18 boys

⇒ **Total weight** of class = 563.5 + 152 = 715.5 kg

⇒ **Required Average weight** = 715.5 ÷ 18

⇒ Average weight = 39.75 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 39.75 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, the new average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Properties of Average

If every observation is increased by a constant k, the **new average** also increases by k. The average always lies between the minimum and maximum values of the data set.

Deviation Concept

Net deviation about the average is always zero. This principle is used to solve **mixture and average** problems faster by assuming a middle value as the mean.</p

questions.question: The temperatures recorded over five consecutive days in a town were: 28°C, 30°C, 32°C, 31°C, and 29°C. What was the average temperature during these five days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume a **base temperature** of 30°C.

Find the **deviations** from 30: (28−30), (30−30), (32−30), (31−30), (29−30) → −2, 0, +2, +1, −1.

Net deviation = (−2) + 0 + (+2) + (+1) + (−1) = 0.

Average = Base + (Net Deviation ÷ Total Days) = 30 + (0 ÷ 5) = 30°C.

**∴ The correct answer is 30°C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Recorded temperatures for **5 consecutive days** are 28°C, 30°C, 32°C, 31°C, and 29°C.

**Formula Used:** Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a94a80a9b8cc7573de0d1901f130e5cd919d357868afeb92f30d04c0446744f.png] 

⇒ Sum of temperatures = 28 + 30 + 32 + 31 + 29

⇒ Sum = 150°C

⇒ Number of days = 5

⇒ Average = 150 ÷ 5

⇒ Average = 30°C

**∴ The correct answer is 30°C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean Property

The algebraic sum of the **deviations** of a set of values from their arithmetic mean is always zero.

Effect of Change in Origin

If a constant value 'k' is added to or subtracted from every observation, the **new average** will also be increased or decreased by 'k'.

Weighted Average

When observations have different levels of importance, the average is calculated as Σwx ÷ Σw, where 'w' is the **weight** assigned to each value 'x'.</p

questions.question: The average of eight numbers is 80. Find the least number if it is (1)/(16) of the sum of the numbers.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **sum** of **eight numbers** = **Average** × **Count** = 80 × 8 = 640.

The **least number** is 1/16 of the total **sum**.

Value = 640 ÷ 16 = 40.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total count of numbers = 8

**Average** of numbers = 80

Condition: **Least number** = 1/16 × **Sum**

**Formula:**

Total Sum = **Average** × Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b7fdfc859674513386f3c531f8e03ade85bc1e19dcae9b1b57913783322bd73c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Sum** of 8 numbers = 80 × 8 = 640

⇒ **Least number** = (1/16) × 640

⇒ **Least number** = 640 ÷ 16

⇒ **Least number** = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

**__Additional Information__**

Concept of Average

The **average** is the central value of a set of data, calculated by Sum ÷ Count.

Summation Property

If the **average** of 'n' numbers is 'x', then their **total sum** is always n × x.

Fractional Parts

To find a specific **fractional part** of a total, multiply the total by the numerator and divide by the denominator.</p

questions.question: A student scored the following marks: 78, 85, 69, and 90 in four subjects. What score is required in the fifth subject to achieve an average of 80 marks across all five subjects?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Target **Average** = 80. Calculate **Net Deviation** of given marks from 80.

Deviations: (78−80) + (85−80) + (69−80) + (90−80) ⇒ −2 + 5 − 11 + 10 = +2.

To keep average at 80, **Net Deviation** must be 0. So, 5th subject deviation must be −2.

5th subject score = Target Average + Required Deviation ⇒ 80 + (−2) = 78.

**∴ The correct answer is 78 marks.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Marks in 4 subjects = 78, 85, 69, 90; Required **Average** for 5 subjects = 80.

**Formula Used:** Total Sum = Average × Number of Observations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/07c15cd6cd79fb63c81a89034765e974799c29a4cce4a1c214afea9b02a21757.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total marks required for 5 subjects = 80 × 5 = 400.

⇒ Sum of marks in 4 subjects = 78 + 85 + 69 + 90.

⇒ Sum of 4 subjects = 322.

⇒ Marks required in 5th subject = Total required marks − Current sum.

⇒ Marks in 5th subject = 400 − 322 = 78.

**∴ The correct answer is 78 marks.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

It is the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. Formula: Mean (μ) = Σx / n.

Net Deviation Rule

The algebraic sum of **deviations** of a set of observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero. This is a powerful tool for solving missing value problems in averages.

New Observation Entry

New Observation = (New Average × New Count) − (Old Average × Old Count).</p

questions.question: The average weight of A, B and C is 45 kg. If the average weight of A and B is 39 kg and that of B and C is 48 kg, then the weight of B (in kg) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Weight of **B** = [Sum of (A + B) + Sum of (B + C)] − Sum of (A + B + C)

Weight of **B** = (2 × 39) + (2 × 48) − (3 × 45)

Weight of **B** = 78 + 96 − 135 = 174 − 135

Weight of **B** = 39 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 39 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of **A, B, and C** = 45 kg

Average weight of **A and B** = 39 kg

Average weight of **B and C** = 48 kg

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6fce19ac9e08c7e35c84a01ead076d2dd57845b78c20fa6c9dd98fdf87cef24d.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Sum of values = **Average** × **Number of observations**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of A + B + C = 3 × 45 = 135 kg

⇒ Total weight of A + B = 2 × 39 = 78 kg

⇒ Total weight of B + C = 2 × 48 = 96 kg

⇒ Sum of (A + B) and (B + C) = 78 + 96 = 174 kg

⇒ This sum can be written as: (A + B + C) + B = 174 kg

⇒ 135 + B = 174

⇒ B = 174 − 135

⇒ B = 39 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 39 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Definition of Average

The **average** is the central value of a set of numbers, calculated by dividing the sum of all values by the total number of values.

Overlap Principle

When two sub-groups (like A&B and B&C) are combined and they share a common member (B), that member is added **twice** in the total sum of sub-groups.

Deviation Method

Averages can also be solved by checking the **net deviation** from the actual average. Sum of deviations from the mean is always zero.</p

questions.question: Ravi spends ₹250 on Monday, ₹300 on Tuesday, ₹275 on Wednesday, ₹325 on Thursday, and ₹350 on Friday. What is his average daily expenditure over these five days?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume a base **Average Expenditure** of ₹300.

Calculate deviations from ₹300: −50, 0, −25, +25, +50.

Sum of deviations = (−50 + 50) + (−25 + 25) + 0 = 0.

Net change in average = 0 ÷ 5 = 0.

Final Average = 300 + 0 = ₹300.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹300.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expenditure on **Monday** = ₹250

Expenditure on **Tuesday** = ₹300

Expenditure on **Wednesday** = ₹275

Expenditure on **Thursday** = ₹325

Expenditure on **Friday** = ₹350

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5f6f3969ddf57fd142e234e19cd12cd39ac9e1c52e58d93aced451e36d37804c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Expenditure = 250 + 300 + 275 + 325 + 350

⇒ Total Expenditure = ₹1500

⇒ Number of Days = 5

⇒ Average Daily Expenditure = 1500 ÷ 5

⇒ Average Daily Expenditure = ₹300

**∴ The correct answer is ₹300.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

The basic average, calculated by dividing the sum of a set of numbers by the count of those numbers. Formula: Average = Σx ÷ n.

Combined Average

The average of two or more groups combined. Formula: Combined Avg = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Average of Consecutive Numbers

For any sequence in Arithmetic Progression (AP), the average is simply (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2.

questions.question: The average weight of 5 students is 60 kg. After a new student joins the group, the average becomes 62 kg. What is the weight of the new student?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Initial average** of 5 students = 60 kg

**Increase** in average after 1 new student = 62 − 60 = 2 kg

**Total students** now = 6

**Weight of new student** = Old Average + (Increase × New Total Students)

⇒ Weight = 60 + (2 × 6) = 60 + 12 = 72 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 72 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of 5 students = 60 kg

Average weight of 6 students = 62 kg

**Formula:** Total Weight = Average × Number of Students

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/81aa4a8bc0680a052f9652386aea8f605cd54c90d6cb2c7112415dfa275bb33c.png] 

⇒ Total weight of 5 students = 5 × 60 = 300 kg

⇒ Total weight of 6 students (including new one) = 6 × 62 = 372 kg

⇒ Weight of the new student = Total weight of 6 students − Total weight of 5 students

⇒ Weight = 372 − 300 = 72 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 72 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Average Formula

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Number of observations.

Net Change in Average

If every value in a set is increased by 'k', the average also increases by 'k'.

Inclusion/Exclusion Rule

New Value = New Average + (Number of previous items × Change in Average).</p

questions.question: The average of 8 numbers is 16. The average of 6 of these numbers is 16. The average of the remaining two numbers is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If the **average** of a **subset** (6 numbers) is equal to the **total average** (16), then the **remaining numbers** must also have the same average to maintain the balance.

Total average = 16

Subset (6) average = 16 ⇒ Deviation = 0

Average of remaining 2 numbers = Total Average + (Net Deviation ÷ 2) = 16 + 0 = 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total numbers (nₜₒₜₐₗ) = 8

Average of 8 numbers (Aₜₒₜₐₗ) = 16

Numbers in first group (n₁) = 6

Average of 6 numbers (A₁) = 16

**Formula Used:**

Sum = Average × Number of observations

Average of remaining = (Total Sum − Sum of known group) ÷ Remaining count

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0e835ef5e90eccb6a1c866a8717d40164696aecd955e2b0de19eaef033bcfe1f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total sum of 8 numbers = 8 × 16 = 128

⇒ Sum of the first 6 numbers = 6 × 16 = 96

⇒ Sum of the **remaining two numbers** = 128 − 96 = 32

⇒ **Average** of the remaining two numbers = 32 ÷ 2 = 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

The combined average of two groups is given by A꜀ₒₘbᵢₙₑd = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Net Deviation Rule

The sum of deviations of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero (Σ(xᵢ − A) = 0).

Property of Constant Average

If a number equal to the average is added or removed from a data set, the average remains unchanged.</p
